R16's own @check has no awareness it was superseded and would keep firing for any untouched tenant, recreating obsolete per-client Finance/Sales/Purchasing/Inventory role clones -- and could re-insert AD_Window_Access rows onto an already-deactivated legacy role (see R27-deactivate-r16-duplicate-roles.sql) if the reference client (GOClient) ever gains a new grant on one of those 4 roles later. R16's .sql file itself stays byte-for-byte untouched (already applied to real tenants, immutable, checksum tracked here) -- this retirement list is the mechanism, not an edit to the fix.

Superseded by the Standard-cost remediation path. R18 seeded Average-cost M_Costing rows (costtype AVA), but Etendo Go now provisions and validates Standard costing rules, whose posting-time lookup requires Standard/legacy Standard costs (costtype STA/ST). Keeping R18 active would add obsolete Average anchors that do not satisfy the current Standard-cost checks and can mislead future investigations. The original .sql file stays byte-for-byte untouched and is skipped through the retirement mechanism.

Superseded by the unified, M_Transaction-sourced anchor fix. R28 only covered Shipment/Receipt (m_inoutline/m_inout); tracing CostingServer.process() and StandardAlgorithm.getTransactionCost() (src/org/openbravo/costing/) showed the SAME @NoStandardCostDefined failure is architecturally reachable from four more document families that also write M_Transaction rows and go through the identical default-case cost lookup: Physical Inventory (m_inventoryline/m_inventory -- confirmed with LIVE gap data, 2 real tenants, 2026-09-03), Internal Movement, Internal Consumption, and Manufacturing/Production (the latter three architecturally exposed but zero live gap rows on any Standard-cost tenant at authoring time). R33-standard-cost-anchor-unified is a strict superset: same target table (m_costing), same guard shape (two-layer idempotency, :client_id scope, IsManual='Y'/IsPermanent='Y'/CostType='STA', warehouse-independent, next-Standard-row bounding), same fallback cost chain, PLUS it fixes a real (if narrow) date-precision bug R28 carried: R28 anchored datefrom at M_InOut.DateAcct, but StandardAlgorithm.getOutgoingTransactionCost() actually looks up the cost at M_Transaction.TrxProcessDate for any tenant with M_Costing_Rule.BackdatedTrxsFixed='N' (all 5 Standard-cost tenants checked) -- R28's anchor only worked because DateAcct <= TrxProcessDate always held (conservative, not exact); R33 reproduces the real per-tenant/per-TrxType date formula. R28's own @check has no awareness it was superseded and would keep running its narrower, less-precise Shipment/Receipt-only query forever if left active alongside R33 -- running both is unnecessary (R33 already covers everything R28 covers) though not unsafe (both guard inserts via the same m_costing NOT EXISTS shape, so no double-anchoring or conflict was observed in side-by-side rolled-back-transaction testing). R28's .sql file stays byte-for-byte untouched (checksum verified against its live bytes in this repo at retirement time); this retirement list is the mechanism, not an edit to the fix. Ledger check (2026-09-03, local dev DB): R28 has ZERO rows in ETGO_DATA_FIX_HISTORY -- it has never actually been run (via node cli/src/data-fixes/run.js) against any real tenant on this DB; only ad-hoc rolled-back-transaction validation touched it. The Experimental GOClient environment could not be reached from this session (network egress blocked, documented SSH tunnel not established) to check its ledger, so this does not rule out R28 having been APPLIED there or elsewhere -- retirement is safe regardless per the framework's own design (an APPLIED-and-superseded fix is exactly what this mechanism is for).

Its effect 2 enforces the ETP-4503 exception that forced multicurrency OFF on the bank-transfer link of PSD2-connected Bank accounts, which ETP-5084 removed: a PIS transfer converts the invoice amount to the account currency before instructing the bank, so a cross-currency transfer is supported and that link is multicurrency like every other payment method. R14's @check has no awareness it was superseded -- on an untouched tenant it would re-apply the removed exception, and on an already-fixed tenant R14 and R29 would fight on every run (R29 turns the link on, R14 turns it back off). R14's .sql stays byte-for-byte untouched (already applied to real tenants, immutable, checksum tracked here). R29 is a strict superset of R14's still-wanted effects 1a + 1b: it enables both multicurrency columns on every method template and every per-account link, with no exception.
